title: Backbone config push withdraws routes to the authoritative DNS servers
source_note: Failure pattern follows the Facebook 2021-10-04 outage: a backbone configuration change withdrew route advertisements for the network hosting the DNS servers, making them globally unreachable and taking everything that resolves a hostname down with them. All services, prefixes, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~15:42 UTC the site is returning 503s for essentially all traffic. Edge load balancers report they cannot reach any backends. No application deploys today. The network team ran a scheduled backbone capacity audit earlier.

signal_lines.msg: scheduled backbone capacity audit starting on core routers
config push withdrew prefixes advertising dns-auth (10.2.0.0/16)
authoritative nameservers unreachable from edge; health checks failing
DNS resolution failed for api.internal (SERVFAIL); 100% of upstream lookups failing
cannot resolve any backend hostnames; serving 503 for all traffic
operator manually re-advertised dns-auth prefixes; resolution recovering

ground_truth.root_cause: A backbone network config push withdrew the route advertisements for the subnet hosting the authoritative DNS servers (dns-auth, 10.2.0.0/16). With the nameservers unreachable, DNS resolution failed globally, so every service that has to resolve a hostname (api-gateway, edge-lb) failed and the edge served 503s for all traffic. Recovery required manually re-advertising the withdrawn prefixes.
evidence_path: network-automation WARN at 15:40: config push withdrew prefixes for dns-auth (10.2.0.0/16)
dns-auth authoritative nameservers become unreachable from the edge at 15:41
api-gateway and edge-lb fail all hostname lookups (SERVFAIL) and serve 503s
recovery after the withdrawn prefixes are re-advertised at ~15:55
ground_truth.fix: Re-advertise the withdrawn prefixes (done). Add a guard to the network automation that refuses a push removing the last route to a critical subnet (DNS, auth), keep an out-of-band management path that does not depend on production DNS, and stagger backbone changes.
